source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"It measures average blood glucose over roughly three months and therefore replaces hemoglobin A1c testing.","B":"It helps assess endogenous insulin secretion or residual beta-cell secretory reserve and must be interpreted in the clinical context.","C":"It determines diabetes type by itself regardless of insulin therapy, clinical history, or other diagnostic information.","D":"It measures renal filtration without providing clinically useful information about endogenous pancreatic insulin secretion."}}
source_row.rationale: C-peptide is secreted with endogenous insulin and can be used to assess residual endogenous insulin secretory reserve in selected insulin-treated patients. It is not an HbA1c substitute and does not classify diabetes by itself.

source_row.stem: An insulin-treated adult has an uncertain diabetes classification, and the clinician orders a serum C-peptide level. What information can this test contribute?
